metadata.case_name: CHUNG TAT HO v. AU HOI LAM SUB-CONTRACTOR LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: less intense construction work or other general labouring work

injuries.description: The left index finger was badly damaged and eventually required amputation above the proximal phalanx.
source: The left index finger was badly damaged and eventually required amputation above the proximal phalanx.
the agreed reports of Princess Margaret Hospital describe the injury to the plaintiff's left index finger as a "severe crush injury" with a fracture of the middle phalanx.
it still causes the plaintiff discomfort and residual pain.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of other single finger

injuries.description: The middle finger was lacerated but fully recovered.
source: The middle finger was lacerated but fully recovered.
The injury to the middle finger comprised lacerations to the right side of that finger.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of finger or thumb

manifestations.description: residual pain in the remaining left index finger stump
osteoporosis of the remaining bone of the left index finger
muscle wasting and grip strength difficulties in the left arm and hand (noted earlier, subsequently returned to within normal ranges)
lacerations to the right side of the middle finger

treatments_received: medical treatment and examination at Princess Margaret Hospital

losses.description: the eventual loss of half of the index finger on that hand is a significant injury
In my judgment, the plaintiff is no longer fit for formworking. He is at too great a disadvantage with persistent pain in his left index finger.
